messages:
maria: heads up — ran into a confusing spot while onboarding a customer. their ops team expects ENV var names like REDWOOD_API_KEY but our Go SDK checks REDWOOD_KEY and the JS SDK checks RW_API_KEY. can we standardize?

sam: oh no. that explains why our sample app docs have three different examples :grimacing: we should pick one and migrate. vote: REDWOOD_API_KEY (explicit product name)

leo: +1 for REDWOOD_API_KEY. also: what's the plan for org/project scoping? some customers expect MULTI-ORG tokens, others want project-scoped tokens. current behavior: header X-Org is optional, project provided as ?project= in query — messy.

ashley: agreed on REDWOOD_API_KEY. for scoping, proposal from security: default token = org-level, add short-lived project-scoped tokens via our token service (rw auth issue) and a header X-Redwood-Project for explicit override. fewer query params.

maria: that sounds sensible. can we make SDKs accept either env var name with a fallback? e.g., check REDWOOD_API_KEY, then RW_API_KEY, then REDWOOD_KEY. we should log a one-time warning if fallback used so we can surface usage stats.

sam: +1 to fallback with one-time warning. also add support for credential rotation hooks so the app can react when token is rotated (webhook or SIGUSR2 style). many infra teams want automatic hot-reload.

leo: implementation idea for JS SDK: process.env lookup example in docs:
```
const key = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || process.env.RW_API_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_KEY;
if (!key) throw new Error('Missing REDWOOD_API_KEY');
// optional scoping header
const headers = { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${key}` }
if (process.env.REDWOOD_PROJECT) headers['X-Redwood-Project'] = process.env.REDWOOD_PROJECT;
```

maria: looks good. can we also add an env var convention for multiple keys (per-service)? e.g., REDWOOD_API_KEY_BILLING, REDWOOD_API_KEY_WORKER. pattern: REDWOOD_API_KEY_<NAME>. that helps service-level rotation.

ashley: love that. security note: env var names should be allowed but we must ensure we never log them. SDKs should redact when printing config. add default exponential retry on 401 with a token-refresh callback hook (so the SDK doesn't blindly retry with stale creds).

sam: can the SDK expose a refresh callback signature? proposed: async function refreshToken(oldToken) -> newToken|null. If null then propagate auth error. SDK should call it only once per request on 401 to avoid thundering herd.

leo: sounds right. also mention TTL on tokens and how rotation happens: our token service will issue tokens with "exp" claim and a rotating-key id. docs should show how to mint ephemeral tokens via CLI: `rw auth token create --project billing --ttl 1h`

maria: i created a draft PR for JS SDK to implement env var fallback + refresh callback + project header. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/402 — could folks glance and leave quick comments? i tried to keep public API minimal.

sdk-bot: CI results for PR #402: 3/4 checks passed, failing test is auth-refresh.spec (timeout flake).

ashley: i'll take the flaky test. quick question: do we want the SDK to expose a helper that auto-watches files for rotation (e.g., when ops writes new key to /.secrets/redwood_api) and reloads? Some teams prefer that over restarting.

sam: yes but opt-in only. make it a small utility watchAndReload({ path, envVarName }) and docs should warn about file perms.

leo: minor doc ask: add a short matrix table listing env var names, header names, CLI flags, and fallback order. that'll reduce support ping volume.

maria: agreed. next steps: 1) land JS PR with fallback + callback; 2) update Go/py SDKs to match behavior; 3) update quickstarts and sample apps to use REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT env vars; 4) announce deprecation timeline for old env names (30 days).

sam: timeline +1. also add telemetry to detect how many apps still use old names so we can extend if needed. make sure telemetry doesn't include key values.

ashley: i'll draft the deprecation message and security checklist. posting to #announcements after approvals.

maria: thanks all. leaving notes in PR. if anyone wants to pair on the Go SDK changes ping me.

leo: ping @maria — i can help tomorrow morning to port the refresh callback pattern to Go.

maria: perfect, thanks! :rocket:
